name: Fragrant Hill Hotel
features: White walls with grey trim and diamond-patterned openings that frame garden views, after Suzhou houses.
award: China: I. M. Pei in China
note: No own English Wikipedia article (redirects to I. M. Pei). Pei began it in 1978 and it opened 17 October 1982; Wikipedia says he sought a third way between modernism and imitation of tradition, with a glass-roofed central atrium. Pei's first building in China. Second photo is the entrance front with a car park.

name: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum
features: Long stair of 392 steps climbs a mountain slope to a granite hall with blue glazed-tile roofs.
note: Built 1926-1929; Wikipedia also credits Poy Gum Lee with completing it after Lü fell ill. First photo looks down the stair from the top; second is the sacrificial hall front.

name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
features: White hall under a blue octagonal roof, raised on two 89-step stairs at the end of a vast square.

photos.file: File:2017-06-29 Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, Zhongzheng District, Taipei.jpg

note: Opened 5 April 1980; designed to echo the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing. Photos are from Category:General views of Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall.

name: National Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
features: Modern hall under a sweeping roof of yellow glazed tiles with upturned corners, a palace-style touch Chiang asked for.

photos.file: File:National Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall 09.jpg

note: Completed 16 May 1972. Wang Da-hong won a public contest; Wikipedia says the design was then modified to stress Chinese characteristics. Photos are in the subcategory Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall (Taipei) from the south. The roof description comes from the photos.

name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall, Guangzhou
features: Octagonal hall under tiered blue-tiled roofs; steel and concrete span 71 m with no columns inside.
note: Built 1929-1931; used as an auditorium and concert hall. Same architect as the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing.

name: Cultural Palace of Nationalities
features: White 13-storey tower crowned with peacock-blue glazed eaves, flanked by low east and west wings.
note: Built September 1959, 67 m high. One of the Ten Great Buildings for the PRC's tenth anniversary. Zhang Bo also designed the Great Hall of the People, already on the wall.

name: Monument to the People's Heroes
features: 38 m obelisk built of 13,000 granite and alabaster blocks, its pedestal ringed by bas-reliefs of modern history.

photos.file: File:Monument to the People's Heroes on Tiananmen Square.jpg

note: Built 1952-1958 and unveiled 1 May 1958. Wikipedia names Liang Sicheng as architect, with some elements by Lin Huiyin. A monument rather than a building; the owner may prefer to leave it out. The two-tier terrace is from the photos.

name: National Palace Museum
features: Palace-style museum set against a hill: green-tiled roofs, yellow walls and white stairs on a long axis.
note: Built March 1964 to August 1965 and opened 12 November 1965; Wikipedia spells the architect Huang Baoyu. Expanded in 1967, 1970, 1984 and 1996, and renovated 2002-2007. Commons category mixes the building with collection objects.

name: Ordos Museum
features: Rounded, edgeless shell wrapped in polished metal louvres, its form drawn from the Gobi Desert.

photos.file: File:康巴什 鄂尔多斯市博物院 01.jpg
File:康巴什 航拍鄂尔多斯市博物院 01.jpg

note: Ordos Museum article gives no year; the Ma Yansong article lists it as 2005-2011, completed. Third photo is aerial. The metal louvre cladding is described from the photos.

name: Leeza SOHO
features: Glass tower split by a 194 m atrium that twists 45 degrees up its height, the world's tallest.
note: Opened 19 November 2019; 207 m tall. First photo is at dusk and shows the twisting atrium slot best.

name: Peace Hotel (Sassoon House)
features: Granite-faced Art Deco block on the Bund, topped by a steep copper pyramid roof gone green.
note: Built 1926-1929 as Sassoon House; now the North Building of the Fairmont Peace Hotel. Wikipedia: reinforced concrete frame, consistent Art Deco scheme inside and out.

name: Ningbo Museum of Art
features: Long grey-brick plinth carrying a timber-slatted steel box, reached by bridges across a moat.
award: China: Wang Shu / Amateur Architecture Studio

photos.file: File:2026-04-19 Ningbo Museum of Art 宁波美术馆 01.jpg
File:2026-04-19 Ningbo Museum of Art 宁波美术馆 02.jpg

note: No own English Wikipedia article; the Amateur Architecture Studio article lists it as completed 2001-05. Features line describes what the photos show.

name: Sheraton Huzhou Hot Spring Resort
features: Horseshoe-shaped ring of white balconied floors rising out of Lake Tai, its hole framing the water.
note: Completed October 2013. Wikipedia is inconsistent on floors (27 in the infobox, 10 in the lead), so floors are left out. Nicknamed the Horseshoe Hotel.

name: Beijing Daxing International Airport Terminal
features: Starfish plan: six curved piers radiate from a central hub, among the world's largest single terminals.
commons_category: Category:Aerial photographs of Beijing Daxing International Airport
note: Opened 25 September 2019; 700,000 m2. Wikipedia credits Zaha Hadid Architects with French planners ADPI; BIAD executed the design. Both photos are aerial views from a plane, which show the starfish plan; I did not find a good ground-level exterior. Main category is Category:Beijing Daxing International Airport.

name: Shenzhen Stock Exchange
features: Tower whose three-storey base is lifted 36 m off the ground, cantilevering over a covered public plaza.

photos.file: File:Shenzhen Stock Exchange in Shenzhen GuangDong China.jpg

note: Built 2008-2013; 245.8 m, 49 floors. Wikipedia names OMA partners Rem Koolhaas, David Gianotten, Ellen van Loon and Shohei Shigematsu. The raised podium is described from the photos (Wikipedia does not mention it). Last photo looks up at the podium's underside.

name: Central Government Complex, Tamar
features: Two towers joined at the top to frame a giant open door, with a park running through to the harbour.

photos.file: File:Central Government Offices and Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region 19-09-2024.jpg
File:Central Government Offices and Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region 14-01-2023(1).jpg

note: In use from 2011. Wikipedia: massing based on the idea of a door always open; Tamar Park passes through to the waterfront. The towers joined at the top are described from the photos. Rocco Yim's Hong Kong Palace Museum is already on the wall.

name: Jardine House
features: 52-storey tower clad in a grid of round windows, which let the structural frame be thinner.

photos.file: File:HK 中環 Central Jardine House facade blue sky July 2020 SS2.jpg

note: Completed 1973, 178.5 m; once the tallest building in Hong Kong and Asia. First photo shows the whole tower from below; the other two are close-ups of the round-window facade.

name: Xiqu Centre
by: Revery Architecture, Ronald Lu and Partners
features: Chinese opera house wrapped in a curved skin of fins, its corners pulled open like a stage curtain.
note: Opened 20 January 2019, in the West Kowloon Cultural District. Only one usable exterior photo on Commons (8064px, a bus partly in front). The facade description is from the photo; Wikipedia does not describe it.

name: Great (Bamboo) Wall House
features: Long low house screened by walls of thin bamboo poles, following the slope near the Great Wall.
award: China: Kengo Kuma in China (Commune by the Great Wall)

photos.file: File:Bamboo House designed by Kengo Kuma at Commune by the Great Wall.jpg

note: Part of the Commune by the Great Wall, villas by twelve Asian architects shown at the 2002 Venice Biennale. Year 2002 from the Kengo Kuma article. Only one exterior photo, 1200x900 (passes the 800px rule); the second photo is the interior bamboo tea room, so the owner may want only the first.

name: Hong Kong Cultural Centre
features: Windowless pink-tiled arts centre on the old railway station site, next to the surviving clock tower.
note: Opened 8 November 1989. Wikipedia names the Public Works Department chief architect José Lei. The windowless walls and curved roof are described from the photos; Wikipedia does not describe the exterior.

name: Hong Kong Design Institute
features: A huge rectangular block held seven storeys up on four towers braced by a steel lattice exoskeleton.
note: Opened autumn 2010 after a 2006 competition. Wikipedia credits Coldefy & Associés, while its Dezeen source names the firm CAAU; check the credit.

name: Oriental Pearl Tower
features: 468 m TV tower: three pillars carry spheres clad in red glass, a design its makers drew from a Tang poem.

photos.file: File:2015 Oriental Pearl Tower, Pudong, Shanghai.jpg

note: Completed 18 November 1994. Wikipedia's infobox gives Shanghai Modern Architectural Design Co. as architect, while the history section says the winning design (1988, from 12 entries) came from the East China Architectural Design Institute; check which credit the owner prefers. The pearls-on-a-plate image is from the Tang poem Pipa xing, as Wikipedia notes.

name: Kaohsiung Music Center
features: Harbourfront music venues: two towers of stacked hexagonal lattice cells beside a low faceted hall.
note: Officially opened 31 October 2021. Wikipedia: designed by the Spanish team MADE IN Architects led by Manuel Monteserín; concert hall for 6,000 and amphitheatre for 10,000, six live houses (the Whales) with green roofs, and an exhibition centre under hexagonal structures. Second photo is at night with coloured lighting.

name: Water-Moon Monastery (Nung Chan Monastery)
features: Long fair-faced concrete hall raised on columns, its screen wall pierced with scripture characters.
note: Wikipedia only says the monastery was reconstructed in 2012 by Kris Yao; it does not describe the building. The pierced screen of characters (the Heart Sutra, as published elsewhere) shows in the first photo; the well-known view across the reflecting pool is not among the Commons files I checked. Weak photos: the owner may prefer to wait for better ones.

name: Taipei Music Center
features: Concert hall under a folded, crystalline metal roof, set apart from a cultural hall and production wing.

photos.file: File:202409 臺北流行音樂中心表演廳 晚間景象A.jpg

note: Opened 5 September 2020; Reiser + Umemoto won the design competition. The first photo is at night with coloured lighting. The second, a better daylight view, is tagged on Commons with the plain Attribution licence (free use with credit, not a CC licence); the owner should decide whether that counts.

name: Shaanxi History Museum
features: Tang-dynasty style rebuilt with modern technology: a central hall with storeyed buildings at the corners.

photos.file: File:2023-10-10 Shaanxi History Museum 陝西歷史博物館 01.jpg

note: Opened 20 June 1991 (built from 1983). The museum article names no architect; the Zhang Jinqiu article lists it among her works. Layout quote from Wikipedia: hall in centre, storied buildings in corners. Second photo is a wide panorama.

name: Shanghai Museum
features: Shaped like an ancient bronze ding: a round top over a square base, for round sky and square earth.

photos.file: File:2008 Shanghai People's Square- Shanghai Museum 1.jpg

note: Inaugurated 12 October 1996 (built from 1993) on People's Square. The ding form and round-sky-square-earth idea are from Wikipedia.

name: 1000 Trees
features: Two stepped mountains of shops and offices on the Suzhou Creek, with trees planted on top of the columns.
note: Wikipedia (Heatherwick Studio article): two mountain-like peaks with trees planted on the buildings; retail, office, events, gallery and hotel; completed in two phases, the first opened 2021. The trees on column tops and Suzhou Creek are from the photos. Type is a mixed-use complex; Workplace is the closest.

name: Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3
features: Vast terminal under a red roof pierced by dozens of triangular windows that bring in daylight.

photos.file: File:T3 of the Capital International Airport ,Beijing China - panoramio.jpg

note: Fully open 26 March 2008; 986,000 m2, then the largest single-phase terminal. Wikipedia credits a consortium of NACO, Foster + Partners and Arup with the Beijing Institute of Architectural Design. First photo is aerial (from a plane); the others show the curved roof edge and the kerbside canopy with red columns.

name: Tianjin Binhai Library
by: MVRDV, Tianjin Urban Planning and Design Institute
features: Terraced white shelves wave up the atrium around a luminous sphere, seen from the park through an eye-shaped opening.
view: front elevation: long louvred box with the eye-shaped opening and the auditorium sphere behind it
note: Opened October 2017. Commons has ten free photos (all CC0, up to 4000px) but every one I looked at is of the interior (shelves and sphere), none of the outside, so I drew the facade. Good interior photos if the owner wants them: File:Tianjin Binhai Library 1.jpg and File:Tianjin Binhai Library 4.jpg (CC0, seen). Simplified: louvre count and the exact size of the eye are approximate. Wikipedia also notes the upper shelves are unreachable and printed with fake book spines.

name: Beijing Railway Station
features: Long station front with two clock towers and pavilion-roofed turrets, blending Chinese roofs with socialist realism.
note: Completed 10 September 1959, opened 4 October 1959; design work chaired by Yang Tingbao and Chen Deng'ao. The turrets on each wing were Zhou Enlai's suggestion, per Wikipedia. Fourth photo is CC BY 3.0 Poland.

name: Pagoda of Fogong Temple (Yingxian Wooden Pagoda)
features: 67 m all-timber pagoda, no nails: five storeys outside, nine inside, held by 54 kinds of bracket sets.
note: Built 1056, renovated 1195. Wikipedia: oldest fully wooden pagoda in China, 67.31 m including platform and steeple; hidden storeys marked outside by balconies. Second photo is a high view over the temple.

name: Tao Zhu Yin Yuan
features: 21-storey tower twisting 90 degrees like a DNA double helix, each floor turned 4.5 degrees, planted with trees.

photos.file: File:20180802 陶朱隱園 Agora Garden, Taipei, Taiwan.jpg
File:Tao Zhu Yin Yuan in the rain 20181101.jpg

note: Completed 2018 (begun 2013); 93.2 m, 21 floors. Wikipedia: about 20,000 trees and shrubs. Also called Agora Garden / Agora Tower.

name: Wah Fu Estate
features: Public housing planned as a self-contained new town by the sea, with its own shops and bus terminus.

photos.file: File:Full of festival vibe in a classic estate!.jpg

note: Built 1967 on a new town concept; 18 blocks completed 1967-1978; designed by Dr Donald Liao, former director of housing. Weak photos: the first shows the estate from the sea, the second is a night festival among the blocks.

name: Xiangshan Visitor Center, Sun Moon Lake
features: Two curved concrete wings with grassed roofs and 34 m canopies, sliding past each other behind a reflecting pool.

photos.file: File:向山遊客中心 Xiangshan Visitor Center - panoramio.jpg

note: Wikipedia: constructed in 2010 by Dan Norihiko; two curved wings with central canopies about 34 m long and 8 m high. Grass roofs and the reflecting water are from the photos.

name: Zhongshan Hall (Taipei Public Hall)
features: Steel-framed hall built to resist fire, quakes and typhoons, faced in green tile, with Islamic-style windows.
note: Built 1932-1936 under Japanese rule as the Taipei Public Hall. Wikipedia: light green tile chosen to be less visible to bombers; Spanish-Islamic window designs. Movement is a judgement call (early modern public hall with historicist detail).

name: Hong Kong Coliseum
features: Indoor arena shaped like an inverted pyramid, its huge sloping bowl lifted over a glazed base.

photos.file: File:HK Hung Hom Hong Kong Coliseum July 2026 N13P 205.jpg

note: Inaugurated 27 April 1983; Wikipedia names Pau Shiu-hung as main designer and describes an inverted pyramid-like construction. Seating rises to 41 m. Brutalism is a judgement call for this concrete megastructure. Second photo is a high view over the Hung Hom station area.

name: Grand Hotel Taipei
features: 87 m, 12-storey hotel in Chinese palace style on Yuanshan hill: vermilion columns, dragon heads on the roof.
note: Main building completed 10 October 1973; same architect as the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall. Wikipedia: one of the world's tallest Chinese classical buildings. Golden roof tiles and hilltop setting are from the photos.

name: Shanghai Exhibition Centre
by: Sergey Andreyev, Chen Zhi, Wang Dingzheng, Cai Xianyu
features: Soviet neoclassical palace: a spired central tower topped by a red star, with curved wings around a forecourt.

photos.file: File:上海展览中心·上海静安.jpg

note: Completed 5 March 1955 as the Sino-Soviet Friendship Building; 110.4 m to the spire. Wikipedia: the tower is modelled on the Admiralty in Saint Petersburg; a thin-shell vaulted hall (30 m span) lies to the north.

name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
features: Grey-white gallery tubes crossing in a 井 (hash) shaped plan, their box-like ends cantilevered out.

photos.file: File:Taipei Fine Arts Museum South Side 20110425.jpg

note: Opened 8 August 1983. Wikipedia: a local interpretation of the Japanese Metabolist movement. The stacked, cantilevered boxes are described from the photos.

name: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Terminal 3
features: 1.6 km terminal in a double honeycomb skin pierced by hexagonal openings; locals call it the giant flying fish.

photos.file: File:Aerial view of Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport.jpg

note: Opened 28 November 2013 (Wikipedia tags the date citation needed); 450,000 m2, 1.6 km long. Wikipedia caption: parametric developed structure and facade. The honeycomb pattern is described from the photos. First two photos are aerial.

name: Shanghai Oriental Art Center
features: Five linked glass-walled halls like petals; from above the plan reads as a butterfly orchid.

photos.file: File:东方艺术中心·上海浦东·俯视.jpg

note: Officially opened 1 July 2005; designed by Paul Andreu with the Huadong Architectural Design & Research Institute. First photo is aerial and shows the petal plan; third is at night. Andreu's National Centre for the Performing Arts in Beijing is already on the wall.

name: East Hall of Foguang Temple
features: Seven-bay Tang timber hall with a hipped roof on deep bracket sets; Liang Sicheng found its date in 1937.
commons_category: Category:East Great Hall of Foguang Temple
note: Built 857 CE; funded by Ning Gongyu and built under the monk Yuancheng (Wikipedia). Seven bays by four, about 34 x 17.7 m. Photos show the corner and eaves brackets well, but none is a clear full front view (the hall sits behind trees on a high terrace).

name: College of Social Sciences, National Taiwan University (Koo Chen-Fu Memorial Library)
features: Single-storey glazed reading room under a skylit roof held up by 88 tree-like columns.

photos.file: File:Koo Chen-Fu Memorial Library, College of Social Sciences, National Taiwan University 20140920.jpg
File:Night in Koo Chen-Fu Memorial Library, National Taiwan University 20141031b.jpg
File:The exterior of the Koo Chen-Fu Memorial Library-2.jpg

note: Year and architect from the Toyo Ito article (2013, College of Social Sciences, NTU). The library is the low pavilion beside the college's main block; the column and roof-disc description is from the photos. Toyo Ito's Taichung theatre and Kaohsiung stadium are already on the wall.

name: Forbidden City
features: Walled and moated palace city of 980 buildings strung along Beijing's north-south axis.

photos.file: File:Views of the Forbidden City from Jingshan Park 1.jpg
File:Beijing Forbidden City Viewed from Jingshan Park (10553754905).jpg
File:The Forbidden City - View from Coal Hill.jpg

note: Built 1406-1420; Wikipedia infobox names Kuai Xiang. 961 x 753 m, 7.9 m wall, 52 m wide moat. All three photos look south from Jingshan Park over the north gate.

name: Anji Bridge (Zhaozhou Bridge)
features: Oldest open-spandrel segmental stone arch: a 37 m span with two small arches in each shoulder.
note: Built 595-605 (Sui dynasty), credited to the craftsman Li Chun. Wikipedia: 28 limestone slabs joined by iron; the side arches lighten the bridge and let floodwater through. A bridge, not a building: the owner may decide whether it belongs on the wall.

name: Potala Palace
features: 13 storeys of white and red palace climbing a hill, on inward-sloping stone walls up to 5 m thick.
note: Begun 1645 on the order of the 5th Dalai Lama; White Palace occupied 1649, Red Palace added 1690-1694, so 1694 is the completion year. No named architect in Wikipedia (Konchog Chophel advised on the site). Political sensitivity: listed under China (CN) as Lhasa is administered by the PRC; the owner may prefer to note Tibet.
